Fun fact:

Fast fashion brands design for the scroll, not the room.

They rely on high-saturation filters and deceptive lighting to sell you a fantasy.

Then you put the garment on in your bedroom and the illusion shatters.

Stop buying clothes that only look good in pixels.

Buy clothes that move, breathe, and survive physical touch.

Friendly reminder that your wardrobe is a system.

If your clothes don't work together, you don't have a style.

You have a pile of fabric that dictates your mood.

True style is a reduction process.

Keep only what fits, what lasts, and what tells the truth about who you are.

Everything else is just clutter you pay to store.

How to know if you have a good garment:

Look at the seams.

If the thread is fraying or the fabric is puckered, you are looking at a liability, not an asset.

Fast fashion is designed to be replaced.

Intentional style is designed to be lived in.

Stop participating in a cycle of waste just to feel a temporary dopamine hit.

Buy once. Buy better.
